subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should trusted inbound-decoration state be a serialized `__openclaw`-owned message metadata contract, and which inbound-decoration owner is responsible for producing it?
rationale: The bug requires a durable provenance boundary, but choosing a generic top-level contract versus a scoped OpenClaw-owned metadata slot changes the long-term message and plugin compatibility surface.

options.title: Use scoped OpenClaw metadata
options.body: Define and produce one internal `__openclaw` inbound-decoration record at the authoritative decoration path, then migrate this PR’s readers to that record.

options.title: Approve a top-level contract
options.body: Accept `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as generic persisted-message fields and document their ownership, serialization, and plugin compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Use scoped OpenClaw metadata
recommendation.body: Define and produce one internal `__openclaw` inbound-decoration record at the authoritative decoration path, then migrate this PR’s readers to that record.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent proposal directly addresses the same durable metadata-boundary choice, though final ownership remains ambiguous from the available history.
